metadata.title: Highway Networks
metadata.authors: Rupesh Kumar Srivastava, Klaus Greff, Jurgen Schmidhuber

nodes.name: Plain feedforward layer
nodes.statement_latex: A plain feedforward layer applies a non-linear transform $H$ parameterized by $\vec{W_H}$ to its input $\vec{x}$ to produce output $\vec{y} = H(\vec{x}, \vec{W_H})$.
nodes.statement_clean: A plain layer in a feedforward network applies a parameterized non-linear transform H to its input.

nodes.name: Highway layer
nodes.statement_latex: A highway layer augments a plain layer with two non-linear transforms $T(\vec{x},\vec{W_T})$ (transform gate) and $C(\vec{x},\vec{W_C})$ (carry gate) so that $\vec{y} = H(\vec{x},\vec{W_H})\cdot T(\vec{x},\vec{W_T}) + \vec{x}\cdot C(\vec{x},\vec{W_C})$.
nodes.statement_clean: A highway layer mixes a non-linear transform of the input with the input itself, weighted by learned transform/carry gates.

nodes.name: Transform gate $T$
nodes.statement_latex: The transform gate is $T(\vec{x}) = \sigma(\vec{W_T}^T \vec{x} + \vec{b_T})$, where $\sigma$ is the logistic sigmoid, $\vec{W_T}$ is the gate weight matrix and $\vec{b_T}$ the gate bias.
nodes.statement_clean: Sigmoid-activated affine gate that controls how much of H(x) is passed through.

nodes.name: Carry gate $C$
nodes.statement_latex: The carry gate is set to $C = \mathbf{1} - T$, so the highway layer reduces to $\vec{y} = H(\vec{x},\vec{W_H})\cdot T(\vec{x},\vec{W_T}) + \vec{x}\cdot(\mathbf{1} - T(\vec{x},\vec{W_T}))$.
nodes.statement_clean: Carry gate is the complement of the transform gate, simplifying the highway equation.

nodes.name: Highway block
nodes.statement_latex: A highway block is the $i^{th}$ unit that computes block state $H_i(\vec{x})$, transform gate output $T_i(\vec{x})$, and block output $y_i = H_i(\vec{x}) T_i(\vec{x}) + x_i (1 - T_i(\vec{x}))$.
nodes.statement_clean: Per-unit version of the highway layer producing a scalar block output.

nodes.name: Information highway
nodes.statement_latex: An information highway is a path in a highway network along which information can flow across several layers without attenuation, enabled by the gating mechanism.
nodes.statement_clean: Path through the network where the carry gate dominates so the input passes through nearly unchanged.

nodes.name: Sigmoid $\sigma$
nodes.statement_latex: $\sigma(x) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-x}},\ x \in \mathbb{R}$.
nodes.statement_clean: The standard logistic sigmoid function used throughout.

nodes.name: Plain layer equation
nodes.statement_latex: $\vec{y} = H(\vec{x}, \vec{W_H})$.

nodes.name: General highway equation
nodes.statement_latex: $\vec{y} = H(\vec{x}, \vec{W_H})\cdot T(\vec{x}, \vec{W_T}) + \vec{x}\cdot C(\vec{x}, \vec{W_C})$.

nodes.name: Simplified highway equation
nodes.statement_latex: $\vec{y} = H(\vec{x},\vec{W_H})\cdot T(\vec{x},\vec{W_T}) + \vec{x}\cdot(\mathbf{1} - T(\vec{x},\vec{W_T}))$.

nodes.name: Boundary behavior of highway layer
nodes.statement_latex: $\vec{y} = \vec{x}$ if $T(\vec{x},\vec{W_T}) = \mathbf{0}$, and $\vec{y} = H(\vec{x},\vec{W_H})$ if $T(\vec{x},\vec{W_T}) = \mathbf{1}$.
nodes.statement_clean: When the transform gate is zero the highway layer is the identity; when it is one the highway layer reduces to the plain layer.
assumptions: $\vec{x}, \vec{y}, H(\vec{x},\vec{W_H})$ and $T(\vec{x},\vec{W_T})$ have the same dimensionality

nodes.name: Jacobian of highway layer at gate extremes
nodes.statement_latex: $\frac{d\vec{y}}{d\vec{x}} = \vec{I}$ if $T(\vec{x},\vec{W_T}) = \mathbf{0}$, and $\frac{d\vec{y}}{d\vec{x}} = H'(\vec{x},\vec{W_H})$ if $T(\vec{x},\vec{W_T}) = \mathbf{1}$.
nodes.statement_clean: At the gate extremes the layer Jacobian is either the identity or the Jacobian of H, which keeps gradients well-conditioned for very deep networks.
assumptions: $\vec{x}, \vec{y}, H, T$ all share the same dimensionality

nodes.name: Sigmoid range prevents exact gate extremes
nodes.statement_latex: Since $\sigma(x) \in (0,1)$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$, the conditions $T = \mathbf{0}$ and $T = \mathbf{1}$ in the boundary identities can never be exactly satisfied.
conclusions: $T(\vec{x}) \in (0,1)^d$ strictly, so the limit cases are approached but never attained

nodes.name: Highway network forward pass
nodes.statement_latex: Forward pass through a highway network: at each layer compute the gated mixture of $H(\vec{x},\vec{W_H})$ and the input $\vec{x}$, weighted by the transform gate $T$ and its complement.
nodes.pseudocode: for l = 1..L: T = sigmoid(W_T,l^T x_l + b_T,l); H = H(x_l, W_H,l); x_{l+1} = H * T + x_l * (1 - T); return x_{L+1}

nodes.name: Negative-bias initialization for highway networks
nodes.statement_latex: Initialize the transform-gate bias $\vec{b_T}$ to a negative value (e.g., $-1, -2, -3, -4$) so the network is initially biased towards \emph{carry} behavior; weights $\vec{W_H}$ follow any standard zero-mean scheme.
output: Initialized highway network biased towards identity routing at start of training
nodes.pseudocode: Set b_T,l = b_0 < 0 for all l; init W_H,l using a standard scheme (e.g. He init); init W_T,l with small zero-mean values.

nodes.name: SGD-with-momentum training of highway networks
nodes.statement_latex: Train highway networks using stochastic gradient descent with momentum, with hyperparameters (learning rate, momentum, decay, activation, gate bias) chosen by random search.
input: Hyperparameters: initial learning rate, momentum, learning-rate decay, activation for $H$ ($\mathrm{ReLU}$ or $\tanh$), transform-gate bias in $[-10, -1]$
nodes.pseudocode: Random-search 40 hyperparameter configs; for each, run SGD with momentum minimizing cross-entropy loss; pick best by training error.

nodes.name: Training of very deep neural networks
nodes.statement_latex: Train feedforward neural networks of very large depth (hundreds of layers) end-to-end with simple gradient-based optimization, despite worsening optimization difficulty as depth grows.

nodes.name: MNIST optimization comparison (10/20/50/100 layers)
nodes.statement_latex: On MNIST, plain and highway networks of depths 10, 20, 50, 100 (1 input layer + 9/19/49/99 hidden + softmax) are trained with SGD+momentum; plain networks degrade sharply with depth while highway networks remain trainable up to 100 layers.
nodes.statement_clean: MNIST experiment showing highway networks remain optimizable as depth grows from 10 to 100, while plain networks degrade.

nodes.name: CIFAR-100 900-layer highway network
nodes.statement_latex: A 900-layer highway network on CIFAR-100 was trained with SGD+momentum; after 80 epochs no signs of optimization difficulty were observed.

nodes.name: Convolutional highway networks vs Fitnets on CIFAR-10
nodes.statement_latex: Convolutional highway networks with ReLU activations and sigmoid gates are trained directly with backpropagation on CIFAR-10 (with random translations), matching or exceeding Fitnet accuracies (e.g., 19-layer Highway 2 achieves $92.24\%$).
nodes.statement_clean: On CIFAR-10, highway networks match or beat Fitnets while being trained directly with backprop (no two-stage hint training).

nodes.name: Internal inspection of 50-layer highway networks
nodes.statement_latex: Inspection of best 50-hidden-layer fully-connected highway networks on MNIST and CIFAR-100 shows transform-gate biases initialized to $-2$ and $-4$ respectively decrease further during training; transform-gate activity is sparse and block outputs form persistent stripes across many layers.
nodes.statement_clean: Visualization of trained highway networks on MNIST and CIFAR-100 shows sparse, selective gating and information-highway stripe patterns.

nodes.name: Inspiration from LSTM gating
nodes.statement_latex: The gating mechanism of highway networks is inspired by Long Short-Term Memory recurrent networks; the negative-bias initialization echoes the proposal of Gers et al. (1999) to bias forget/output gates so as to bridge long-range temporal dependencies early in learning.

nodes.name: Dimensionality matching for highway layers
nodes.statement_latex: When changing representation size, replace $\vec{x}$ with a sub-sampled or zero-padded $\hat{\vec{x}}$, or insert a plain layer for the dimensionality change and continue stacking highway layers (the choice used in this study).

nodes.name: Convolutional highway construction
nodes.statement_latex: Convolutional highway layers use weight-sharing and local receptive fields for both $H$ and $T$; zero-padding is used to keep block-state and transform-gate feature maps the same size as the input.

nodes.name: Initialization independence from $H$
nodes.statement_latex: Negative-bias initialization of $\vec{b_T}$ is sufficient for learning to proceed in very deep highway networks across various zero-mean initial distributions of $\vec{W_H}$ and various activation functions for $H$ (e.g., ReLU, tanh).

nodes.name: Transform-gate biases used for selectivity, not shutdown
nodes.statement_latex: On CIFAR-100 the trained transform-gate biases form a depth-dependent gradient that is inversely correlated with mean gate activity, indicating the strong negative biases at low depths make gates more selective rather than simply shutting them down.

nodes.name: Proof of boundary behavior of highway layer
nodes.statement_latex: By case analysis: substitute $T = \mathbf{0}$ and $T = \mathbf{1}$ into the simplified highway equation $\vec{y} = H\cdot T + \vec{x}\cdot(\mathbf{1}-T)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Jacobian limits
nodes.statement_latex: Differentiate the boundary identities of Proposition PrP217.1 with respect to $\vec{x}$.

nodes.name: Substitute $T = \mathbf{0}$ into highway equation
nodes.statement_latex: Plug $T(\vec{x},\vec{W_T}) = \mathbf{0}$ into $\vec{y} = H(\vec{x},\vec{W_H})\cdot T + \vec{x}\cdot(\mathbf{1} - T)$ to obtain $\vec{y} = H(\vec{x},\vec{W_H})\cdot\mathbf{0} + \vec{x}\cdot\mathbf{1} = \vec{x}$.

nodes.name: Substitute $T = \mathbf{1}$ into highway equation
nodes.statement_latex: Plug $T(\vec{x},\vec{W_T}) = \mathbf{1}$ to obtain $\vec{y} = H(\vec{x},\vec{W_H})\cdot\mathbf{1} + \vec{x}\cdot\mathbf{0} = H(\vec{x},\vec{W_H})$.

nodes.name: Differentiate highway equation at $T = \mathbf{0}$
nodes.statement_latex: From $\vec{y} = \vec{x}$ at $T = \mathbf{0}$ (Proposition PrP217.1), differentiating with respect to $\vec{x}$ yields $\frac{d\vec{y}}{d\vec{x}} = \vec{I}$.

nodes.name: Differentiate highway equation at $T = \mathbf{1}$
nodes.statement_latex: From $\vec{y} = H(\vec{x},\vec{W_H})$ at $T = \mathbf{1}$ (Proposition PrP217.1), differentiating yields $\frac{d\vec{y}}{d\vec{x}} = H'(\vec{x},\vec{W_H})$.

nodes.name: Compute transform gate $T$
nodes.statement_latex: $T \leftarrow \sigma(\vec{W_T}^{\top}\vec{x}_l + \vec{b_T})$.

nodes.name: Compute non-linear transform $H$
nodes.statement_latex: $H \leftarrow H(\vec{x}_l, \vec{W_{H,l}})$ (typically affine + non-linearity).

nodes.name: Combine via gated mixture
nodes.statement_latex: $\vec{x}_{l+1} \leftarrow H \cdot T + \vec{x}_l \cdot (\mathbf{1} - T)$.

nodes.name: Loop over layers $l = 1,\ldots,L$
nodes.statement_latex: Repeat the gate, transform, and mixture steps for $l = 1,\ldots,L$, then return $\vec{x}_{L+1}$.

nodes.name: Set negative gate bias $\vec{b_T} = b_0$
nodes.statement_latex: For each layer $l$, set $\vec{b_{T,l}} = b_0$ with $b_0 \in \{-1,-2,-3,-4,\ldots\}$ (negative).

nodes.name: Initialize $\vec{W_H}$ via standard zero-mean scheme
nodes.statement_latex: Initialize $\vec{W_H}$ using a standard zero-mean scheme such as He (2015); initialize $\vec{W_T}$ similarly with small zero-mean values.

nodes.name: Random search over hyperparameters
nodes.statement_latex: Sample 40 hyperparameter configurations: initial learning rate, momentum, learning-rate decay, activation for $H$ ($\mathrm{ReLU}$ or $\tanh$), and transform-gate bias in $[-10, -1]$.

nodes.name: Run SGD+momentum for each configuration
nodes.statement_latex: For each sampled configuration, train the network end-to-end with SGD with momentum, minimizing cross-entropy on the training set.

nodes.name: Select best configuration
nodes.statement_latex: Return the trained network achieving the lowest training cross-entropy across the 40 random-search runs.
